... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Bangladesh, on the other hand, showed a good fight, but their poor show with the bat in the first innings is proving to be the difference in this game. Mehidy Hasan was the standout batter for them with a magnificent 97 agonizingly falling short of a hundred. He was well-supported by debutant Jaker Ali as well who notched up his maiden Test fifty. There were a couple of good contributions Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Mushfiqur Rahim that helped their total over 300 taking the lead over 100 runs, but not much more than that. Now, the bowlers will need to make some early inroads to make a game out of this and put pressure on the visitors.

Take a bow, Kagiso Rabada! He finishes with his best figures in Test cricket against Bangladesh and South Africa needs 106 runs to go up in the series. The Proteas started well picking up a couple of wickets early, but after that had to grind it out for every wicket. Aiden Markram had to work really hard with his tactics and field positions, but in the end, he will be happy with the effort of his bowlers. Keshav Maharaj was crucial in getting those 3 important wickets in the middle order while Wiaan Mulder chipped in with one as well.

OUT! TAKEN AT SLIPS! Oh..no! Mehidy Hasan just misses out on a well-deserved hundred here! Kagiso Rabada wraps things up with a six-wicket haul. He lands this on a hard length and just around off, Mehidy Hasan backs away and tries to ramp it away to get to the ton. But he only manages to get an outside edge towards slip cordon where Wiaan Mulder takes a fantastic catch. Bangladesh have been bowled out for 307!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for Day 4! Bangladesh will hope to extend their lead further and give something to their bowlers to bowl at. Mehidy Hasan and Nayeem Hasan are the overnight batters for them. South Africa as expected takes the second new ball straightaway and hands it to Kagiso Rabada who will start the attack for them. Let's play...

A spirited effort from the Bangladesh lower order saw them avoid an innings defeat but they are still behind in the game. The lead is just 81 and it’s still some runs away from being a competitive score. Mehidy Hasan is still out there and Nayeem Hasan has played well along with him so far. The former will be eying a ton and the job of the latter is to continue to hang around. They’ll seriously hope they can take their lead past the 150-run mark and then challenge the Proteas in the fourth innings. South Africa, on the other hand, will hope they can make quick work of the lower order as anything above 150 could be a tricky chase. They will have the option to take the second new ball from the start, and with Kagiso Rabada in fine form, he could wrap things up sooner rather than later. Day 4 could either end quickly or it could turn out to be very interesting. The first session can indicate a lot. Stay tuned.

Hello and a warm welcome folks! We have seen it all in this first Test. The bowlers dominating on the first day and then the batters from both sides showing good determination and resilience in the next two days to make things a lot interesting. As we head into Day 4 which could probably be the final day, South Africa will feel that they still hold the cards, but Bangladesh might have other ideas just as they showed on Day 3.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from a shortened Day 3 of this Test. Bangladesh have shown great determination and are leading by 81 runs which no one would have expected given their showing with the bat in the first innings. They will want to add as much as possible and set up a big target while South Africa will look to wrap things up in the morning session itself. Day 4 promises to be another eventful one and there is a huge chance that we will get a result. As we lost a lot of overs and time again, it will begin early at 3.45 am GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

South Africa, on the other hand, will be really disappointed with their performance. Kagiso Rabada set the tone with a couple of wickets early on while Keshav Maharaj also picked up one. At that point, Bangladesh were still trailing by just under 100 runs and with only 4 wickets in hand. However, after that early burst, the visitors failed to build on that and allowed the hosts to not only get back in the game but also put pressure back on South Africa. They finally got the breakthrough which was provided by Keshav Maharaj who was the only spinner who looked threatening as Dane Piedt was pretty expensive. Now, with the second new ball available, they will surely be looking to take that at the start of Day 4, and get these three wickets quickly as chasing something over 150 on this wicket will not be easy at all.

Bangladesh were rocked early when they lost both the overnight batters, Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Mushfiqur Rahim in the same over and were starring at the barrel of an innings defeat. However, Mehidy Hasan and Jaker Ali had other ideas and started the fight back. Initially, they looked to survive and ride the storm, but once they started to play their shots, there was no stopping them. They dominated proceedings and not only chipped away into the lead but helped them go past it with the biggest partnership of the match. Ali notched up his fifty on debut, but could not stick around for long after that. Mehidy and Nayeem Hasan then got together and frustrated South Africa making sure they did not lose any more wickets, and were also helped by bad light and rain that did not allow the Proteas to attack them with the second new ball.

Bad news folks! With the lights showing no signs of improving, the umpires have decided to call STUMPS ON DAY 3. It was really a stop-start kind of a day, but a good one for Bangladesh as they have put themselves in a position from where they can even think of winning this Test. South Africa, after making early inroads would have thought that they could finish the game early, but some inconsistent bowling along with an incredible fight with the bat from the hosts have kept this match alive.

Aiden Markram needs to make a decision whether to stay on and bowl only spin or take the second new ball and bring Kagiso Rabada into the attack. He is having that discussion with the umpires who still deem it is not safe for a pacer to bowl. Mehidy Hasan and Bangladesh look reluctant to go, but as Markram requests he wants to bowl a pacer, the umpires cannot do anything except STOP PLAY DUE TO BAD LIGHT. This is not the end of Day 3, and we hope that the light gets better so that we can at least get some more action.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final session! The players are making their way out to the middle now. Nayeem Hasan and Mehidy Hasan to resume the batting for Bangladesh. The umpires have informed South Africa that the light is not good enough for a pacer to bowl. Surprisingly, it is Aiden Markram who will start proceedings with the ball. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...
WE HAVE A START TIME! PLAY WILL RESUME AT 9 AM GMT! The umpires had a little inspection, and they are happy with the outfield. Credit to the ground staff for preparing it pretty quickly as well.

UPDATE - 8.40 am GMT - Some positive news! The covers are being taken off now as the rain has stopped fully. The Super Soppers are also working to dry the outfield and the ground staff are working hard to get it ready as soon as possible. The only thing is that the blue skies have faded and it is pretty dark out there. The floodlights are on and whenever we get back out on the field, light could be a factor. Fingers crossed!

SESSION SUMMARY - 66 runs and 1 wicket in 17 overs! We only managed to get around an hour of play in this session, but it was pretty eventful. Firstly, Bangladesh went ahead for the first time in this game and made sure that South Africa had to bat in the fourth inning. The duo of Mehidy Hasan and Jaker Ali picked up from where they left in the first session, with the latter nothing up a maiden Test fifty on debut. However, after a lot of grinding, Keshav Maharaj finally broke the 138-run stand which was the highest of this game, giving the Proteas some hope. Maharaj looked threatening and almost got Nayeem Hasan as well only to be outdone by a review. Mehidy holds the key for them batting on 77 off 155. With a lead of 65 runs and only 3 wickets in hand, the hosts still have a lot of work to do, but the way they have fought back in this game, we cannot rule them out yet.

EARLY TEA ON DAY 3 HAS BEEN TAKEN! The umpires have decided to use this delay as Tea time and with the rain slowing down a bit, hope that we can be back in action after the break. There is not much movement from the groundstaff but we can that the sky is clearing up and it will not be surprising if we see some cricket sooner rather than later.

UPDATE - 8 am GMT - The visuals show that it is still raining and the covers are firmly in place. It looks like we are in for a longer delay, but the good thing is that there are some blue skies above the ground and hopefully, this is just a passing shower. Stick with us for more news.

Oh..no! It has started to drizzle here in Mirpur! The covers and the hessian are coming on quickly and as we write this, the drizzle has turned into a heavy rainfall. We can see the players making their way out of the ground with the Test match hanging in the balance at the moment. Also, when we come back, South Africa will have the option of taking the second new ball which could prove to be decisive in this game. Stay tuned for further updates.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session! The players are already out in the middle now. Jaker Ali and Mehidy Hasan are two batters for Bangladesh looking to extend their excellent partnership. Keshav Maharaj to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

South Africa on the other hand, will be eager to break this stand which is worth 89 runs now and has really frustrated the Proteas. Aiden Markram at the start of the session with everything going their way, would not have thought about batting again in this game, but that's the nature of this sport as anything can happen. South Africa would really not mind this break as the momentum is completely with the hosts. They would hope to come out and begin as they began the day. Can they end Bangladesh's fightback quickly after the Lunch? Join us in about 40 minutes or so to find out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 100 runs and 3 wickets in 35.5 overs! That’s a fine fightback by Bangladesh! At one stage, an innings defeat looked certain. They lost three in quick succession this morning. Kagiso Rabada was on fire as he got two and it was Keshav Maharaj who got the other. However, Mehidy Hasan and Jaker Ali have batted really well after that. Mehidy was the star with the bat. He’s scored a fine half-ton and is not done yet. Jaker Ali is nearing one and the hosts will hope they can continue the good work. They trail by just the one and Bangladesh would want this partnership to continue for long.
Flatter, full and on middle, Mehidy Hasan sweeps it towards deep square leg for a single. Bangladesh trails by just a solitary run now. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 3!

Jubilation among the Proteas and they are inching closer to the win now!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start Day 3! The South African players are in a huddle and then spread out to take their respective field positions. There was a bit of rain around earlier, but thankfully we are starting on time, and the Proteas pacers will enjoy the overcast conditions. Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Mushfiqur Rahim to resume the batting for Bangladesh, Dane Piedt to finish his incomplete over. Let's play...

Bangladesh showed improvement, but they still have a mountain to climb to get back into this game. Their bowlers were inconsistent, conceding nearly 200 runs for the last four wickets, something that might prove costly. Hasan Mahmud was impressive, leaving them to wonder if playing just one seamer was the right call. While their spinners have had assistance from the pitch, the South African pacers showed there's something in it for them too. Bangladesh were in early trouble, losing two quick wickets, but Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Najmul Hossain Shanto steadied the ship before the captain's dismissal. Now, much rests on the set opener and Mushfiqur Rahim, who's adopted an aggressive approach. They'll look to close the lead quickly, but it won’t be easy. South Africa knows that an early breakthrough will put them firmly in control. Stay tuned for all the action coming up!

After battling tough conditions on Day 1, South Africa shifted gears on Day 2, opting to score runs instead of merely surviving. Kyle Verreynne stole the show with a brilliant century, and his 119-run partnership with Wiaan Mulder, who also registered his maiden Test fifty, proved vital. Dane Piedt’s handy contribution further pushed the lead past 200. Kagiso Rabada then rattled Bangladesh early with two quick wickets, but the Proteas struggled to maintain pressure, allowing the hosts to regain some footing. Keshav Maharaj eventually provided the breakthrough, but a few dropped chances and fading light brought an early end to Day 2.

Hello and a warm welcome, everyone! It’s 'Moving Day' in this first Test between South Africa and Bangladesh, and it might just turn out to be the final day of the contest. The Proteas are firmly in control, but they can't afford to underestimate the hosts, who showed real grit on Day 2 to keep themselves in the game.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from an entertaining Day 2 of this Test. Now, we move into the 'Moving Day' where to be honest with how things are going, we may even see a result. South Africa will be looking to make early inroads while Bangladesh needs to bat sensibly and bat long to fully make a comeback in this match. Day 3 is scheduled for an early start again at 3.45 am GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Bangladesh, on the other hand, will be relieved of how things panned out on Day 2. It took them almost two sessions to pick the last four wickets and that was a big factor that they conceded the big lead. Hasan Mahmud was excellent with the ball and provided the big breakthrough while Mehidy Hasan wrapped things up with a couple. While batting, Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque failed to make any impact but skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mahmudul Hasan Joy steadied things nicely. After the dismissal of Shanto, Mushfiqur Rahim came in and played his shots showing attacking intent which is probably the best way to play on this pitch, and along with Joy chipped away into the lead. They still trail by 101 runs, and have a lot of work to do, but will take a lot of confidence from their performance here into the 'Moving Day'.

South Africa are still ahead in this game, but Bangladesh have fought back nicely to keep themselves in the picture. After seeing what happened on Day 1, everyone would thought that it would be even more difficult batting on this wicket. However, the wicket has settled down a bit, and despite the spinners getting some help, a few batters from both sides showed that if you spend time on it, you will score runs. Earlier it was Kyle Verreynne's fantastic century that helped South Africa take a lead of 202 runs, and then they started with a bang with the ball as well. Kagiso Rabada picked up a couple of early wickets, but after that, they struggled a bit and it was Keshav Maharaj in the final session who got the breakthrough getting rid of the opposition skipper. The Proteas did miss out on a couple of opportunities towards the end and will want to improve on that when they take the field again.

The two umpires bring out the light meter and check for the fading light with the reading they had taken on Day 1! Oh dear, they deem it unfit and ask the players to walk off! Well, it does not take them long to confirm that IT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2. Once again, we have lost overs and more than what we did on the first day. However, this game has moved at a very fast pace, and with three days remaining both teams are very much in it to win it.

MISSED STUMPING! A rush of blood almost costs Mahmudul Hasan Joy his wicket here. This is tossed up, full and on middle, Joy skips down the track for a wild slog across the line but misses it completely. The ball hits a rough and bounces a bit more as the keeper, Kyle Verreynne has to collect it near his chest height and by the time he breaks the stumps, Joy dives back to get his bat inside. It is sent upstairs to check to be absolutely sure. The third umpire sees a lot of replays, and there is a moment when the bat is in the air and the lights go off on the bails. But before the bat went up in the air, Mahmudul Hasan Joy managed to get some part of it behind the crease which saved him. A really close call but he survives!

Coming into bat, Bangladesh needed a solid start but it was far from that. After a couple of quiet overs, Kagiso Rabada came in and struck twice in one over to put the hosts in a spot of bother.  Earlier in the session, the Bangladeshi bowlers found it tough to take the last couple of wickets and ended up conceding a lot of runs that could prove to be defining in this game. However, Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Najmul Hossain Shanto made sure that they rode the storm and remained unfazed till the end of the session. The hosts are still trailing by 183 runs and they need a few partnerships to get back in the game, while South Africa will be hoping to pick more wickets in the final session and get closer to victory. Join us in about 20 minutes to see how the third session unfolds.
